rfi.title: Corsica autonomy plan clears first hurdle in divided French parliament
rfi.description: Corsica’s proposed autonomy within the French Republic has cleared its first parliamentary hurdle, with lawmakers backing a constitutional reform that could give the island new powers while leaving key state authority in Paris.

rfi.title: EU tightens migration rules, eyes strategic enlargement in Balkans
rfi.description: The European Union has reached a deal on tougher migration rules that would allow countries to set up so-called “return hubs” outside the bloc, a move hailed by supporters as a practical answer to stalled deportations, but denounced by rights groups as a dangerous step towards offshore detention. Meanwhile, the question of EU enlargement is also on the cards at a Western Balkans summit.

rfi.title: EU unveils plan to cut dependence on US and Asian technology

rfi.title: Tanzania's Hassan makes historic Russia visit amid frayed ties with West
rfi.description: Tanzanian President Samia Suluhu Hassan begins a three-day state visit to Russia on Wednesday – the first official trip by a Tanzanian head of state to Moscow since 1969 – as her government faces growing criticism from Western countries over violence linked to the country's 2025 elections.

rfi.title: Faye appoints cabinet despite Sonko's Pastef boycott threat
rfi.description: Senegal's President Bassirou Diomaye Faye has appointed a new government, despite an initial threat by his own party to boycott the process. Pastef, led by former prime minister Ousmane Sonko, said it would not participate, citing disagreements over the cabinet's composition, but five of its members ultimately appeared on the final list.

rfi.title: El Nino threat grows as Europe prepares for another hot summer
rfi.description: The warming El Nino climate phenomenon is likely to develop by the end of August, the United Nations' weather agency said, raising the risk of extreme weather as Europe faces another summer on the front line of climate change.

rfi.title: Players to watch: England's Harry Kane is chasing history
rfi.description: Harry Kane will play for England at a third World Cup this summer, at the age of 32. In the second instalment of a five-part series on players to watch at the 2026 tournament in the United States, Mexico and Canada, RFI looks at the World Cup career of England's record goalscorer.

rfi.title: Africa's finest: The Elephants are back and this time they mean business
rfi.description: Cote d'Ivoire enter the first 48-team World Cup as Africa's sixth best side in the Fifa rankings. In the third instalment of a nine-part series on African squads at the tournament, RFI looks at a nation making its fourth appearance.

rfi.title: First contact: Cape Verde's rise to the global stage
rfi.description: Cape Verde will make its World Cup debut at the 2026 tournament in the United States, Mexico and Canada. In the third instalment of a four-part series, RFI looks at the journey of the second smallest nation after Curaçao to qualify for the competition in its 96-year history.

The government said confirmed Ebola cases had risen to 321.

rfi.title: French health minister promises fast track access to mental health for youth
rfi.description: France's Health Minister Stéphanie Rist announced on Tuesday that the government would fast-track access to mental health appointments for young people. She promised that those identified by staff in the national education system as having mental health problems would be seen by a professional within 24 to 48 hours.

france24fr.title: La croissance mondiale menacée par le conflit au Moyen-Orient
france24fr.description: Dans son rapport trimestriel, l'OCDE explique que l'économie mondiale est sous pression en raison de la guerre au Moyen-Orient : si aucun accord de paix n'est conclu cette année, plusieurs pays pourront rapidement entrer en récession ou s'en rapprocher. L'organisation a donc revu ses prévisions de croissance à la baisse et table désormais sur une hausse du PIB comprise entre 2,1 % et 2,8 % cette année.

france24fr.title: L'Intelligence artificielle est-elle hors de contrôle ?
france24fr.description: Donald Trump a signé, mardi, un décret très attendu instituant un encadrement de l'IA aux États-Unis, au nom de la cybersécurité. Le texte entend notamment protéger les systèmes informatiques du pays face à des modèles d'IA désormais capables de repérer et d'exploiter des failles à une vitesse inédite. La start-up américaine Anthropic a d'ailleurs développé un nouveau modèle d'IA : Mythos, encore en phase de test. Il s'est révélé encore plus performant que ses créateurs ne l'imaginaient.

france24fr.title: Le retour d'El Niño aggrave la catastrophe climatique
france24fr.description: L'Organisation Météorologique Mondiale a confirmé le retour d'El Niño dès cet été. Un phénomène dont l'intensité reste à définir mais qui pourrait être assez intense. Cet événement naturel va réchauffer l'atmosphère pendant un an, aggravant un peu plus les effets du réchauffement climatique d'origine humaine. On s'attend par endroit à des sécheresses et ailleurs à des pluies diluviennes avec des conséquences notamment sur l'agriculture et donc la sécurité alimentaire mondiale.

france24fr.title: Royaume-Uni : l'indignation monte autour de l'arrestation d'un étudiant poignardé à mort
france24fr.description: Indignation au Royaume-Uni : Henry Nowak, un étudiant de 18 ans, mortellement blessé à l’arme blanche, a été menotté alors qu’il agonisait, après que son assaillant a accusé à tort sa victime d’une attaque raciste.

france24fr.title: Sénégal : Ousmane Sonko explique le refus du Pastef au gouvernement
france24fr.description: 🇸🇳 Au Sénégal, l’ancien Premier ministre Ousmane Sonko a expliqué, mardi 2 juin, les raisons du refus du Pastef de participer au nouveau gouvernement. Une prise de parole qui intervient au lendemain de l’annonce de la composition de l’équipe gouvernementale par son successeur, Ahmadou Al Aminou Mohamed Lô.

france24fr.title: Roland-Garros : Kostyuk contre Andreeva, une demi-finale sur fond de guerre en Ukraine
france24fr.description: Après son quart de finale face à sa compatriote Elina Svitolina, Marta Kostyuk est devenue la première Ukrainienne à se qualifier pour une demi-finale de Roland-Garros. Le duel face à la Russe Mirra Andreeva s'annonce brûlant alors que son adversaire prend régulièrement la parole sur l'invasion de son pays.

france24fr.title: La Tour Eiffel comme vous ne l'avez jamais vue : immersion dans la Dame de Fer
france24fr.description: Plongez dans l'histoire du monument le plus célèbre de France. C'est ce qui est proposé en ce moment au pied de la Tour Eiffel : une expérience immersive qui nous emmène en 1889, lors de l’Exposition Universelle. Une visite inédite validée par les descendants de Gustave Eiffel permet de revivre sa construction.

france24fr.title: L'aéroport de Koweït City en feu après un attaque iranienne, au moins un mort et 63 blessés
france24fr.description: L'aéroport international du Koweït a été touché par des drones iraniens, faisant au moins un mort et plusieurs blessés. L’attaque a provoqué une suspension du trafic et encore davantage fragilisé le cessez-le-feu en place entre les États-Unis et l'Iran. Récit de Nina Masson et Solange Mougin.

france24fr.title: Deux secouristes tués dans une frappes israélienne sur le sud du Liban
france24fr.description: Une frappe israélienne a touché mercredi les environs de Beyrouth. L’armée poursuit également ses raids dans le sud du Liban, où au moins six personnes ont été tuées, dont deux secouristes. Récit de Nina Masson et Maxence Oudotte.

france24fr.title: Le prodige Français Victor Wembanyama à quatre victoires d'un premier titre NBA
france24fr.description: Victor Wembanyama jouera dans la nuit de mercredi à jeudi sa première finale NBA avec les San Antonio Spurs, à seulement 22 ans, face aux Knicks de New York. Après sept matchs d’anthologie, le prodige français a reçu ce dimanche le titre de meilleur joueur des finales de la Conférence Ouest. Un récit de Jules Boiteau.

france24fr.title: Masculinistes, suprémacistes, complotistes : le "Davos" russe en croisade contre l'Occident "dépravé"

Un étrange mélange de personnalités aussi controversées que le masculiniste Andrew Tate est censé donner une bonne image de la Russie de Vladimir Poutine.

france24fr.title: Wim Wenders retire "Faux Mouvement", film de 1975 montrant Nastassja Kinski nue adolescente
france24fr.description: Le réalisateur allemand Wim Wenders a annoncé mercredi retirer son film "Faux Mouvement", sorti en 1975, en raison d'une scène où l'actrice Nastassja Kinski, alors âgée de 13 ans, est montrée seins nus. L'actrice allemande luttait depuis dix ans pour faire supprimer la scène du long-métrage.

france24fr.title: Présidentielle en Colombie : icône de la gauche ou milliardaire soutenu par Trump ?

france24fr.title: Assaut du Capitole : Trump renonce finalement à créer un fonds d'indemnisation pour les condamnés
france24fr.description: Donald Trump a finalement renoncé à son projet "anti-instrumentalisation" de la justice, tout juste créé. Cette annonce survient après la décision d’un tribunal d’en geler le fonds. Les démocrates ont dénoncé une "caisse noire" destinée à rétribuer les partisans de Donald Trump, y compris des personnes condamnées pour l'assaut du Capitole, sanctuaire de la démocratie américaine, le 6 janvier 2021. france24fr.title: Au Japon, un ours attaque un ouvrier devant son usine, casse une porte vitrée, puis disparaît
france24fr.description: Que feriez-vous si vous faisiez face à un ours ? La question vous paraît peut-être saugrenue, mais elle se pose de plus en plus fréquemment dans le quotidien des japonais. Le pays a enregistré mardi une nouvelle attaque, dans deux usines d'un quartier résidentiel. L'année dernière, treize personnes sont mortes suite à une confrontation avec un ours au Japon… un record. france24fr.title: Russie : des drones ukrainiens endommagent des sites militaires à Saint-Pétersbourg

spiegel.description: Thomas Müller und Lisa Müller haben sich getrennt. Er wechselte vergangenen Sommer von München nach Kanada, sie blieb in Bayern. Schon lange wurde über die Beziehung der beiden spekuliert.

spiegel.title: Die Portugiesen jubeln, die Österreicher feiern. Und Deutschland? Ist blamiert
spiegel.description: Außenminister Johann Wadephul wollte Deutschland einen Sitz im Uno-Sicherheitsrat sichern. Doch er scheiterte. Ist das die Quittung für die Außenpolitik der Bundesregierung?

spiegel.title: Konservative und Rechtsextreme koalieren in weiterer spanischer Region
spiegel.description: In Spanien weiten die konservative Volkspartei (PP) und die rechtsextreme Vox ihre Strategie regionaler Bündnisse aus, jetzt in Kastilien und León. Die Parteien kritisieren die liberale Einwanderungspolitik der Regierung scharf.

spiegel.title: Ebola in DR Kongo laut WHO weiter außer Kontrolle
spiegel.description: WHO-Chef Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus hat die von Ebola betroffene Region in der Demokratischen Republik Kongo besucht. Die Krankheit habe immer noch einen Vorsprung, sagt er – auch wegen der hohen Dunkelziffer.

spiegel.title: NBA-Finals 2026: Das müssen Sie zu den NBA-Finals wissen
spiegel.description: Die New York Knicks und die San Antonio Spurs spielen ab heute Nacht um die NBA-Meisterschaft. Kann man das in Deutschland schauen? Kommt es zum Showdown zwischen Donald Trump und New Yorks Bürgermeister Mamdani? Der Überblick.

spiegel.title: Großbritannien: Nachwahl überschattet von Skandal um Fall Henry Nowak
spiegel.description: Ein 18-Jähriger ist in Southampton erstochen worden, die Polizei verwechselte Täter und Opfer. Rechte wie der Populist Nigel Farage schüren Wut. Nun könnte der Fall den Machtkampf um Premier Starmer verschärfen.

spiegel.title: Wim Wenders und Nastassja Kinski: Streit über Nacktszenen in »Falsche Bewegung«
spiegel.description: Wim Wenders wollte seinen Film »Falsche Bewegung« lieber aus dem Verkehr ziehen, als die Nacktaufnahmen der 13-jährigen Nastassja Kinski herauszuschneiden. Warum Regisseure in den Siebzigerjahren oft wenig Skrupel hatten, Minderjährige zu sexualisieren.

spiegel.title: Trumps Kandidat Randy Feenstra verliert Gouverneursvorwahl der Republikaner in Iowa
spiegel.description: Es ist die erste Niederlage für einen von Trump unterstützten Kandidaten seit Langem: Randy Feenstra hat die Gouverneursvorwahl der Republikaner in Iowa knapp verloren.

spiegel.title: Uno-Sicherheitsrat: So reagiert die deutsche Politik auf die Niederlage
spiegel.description: Eine blamable Niederlage, eine große Enttäuschung: Deutschlands Bewerbung um einen nicht ständigen Sitz im Uno-Sicherheitsrat ist gescheitert. Deutsche Politiker reagieren scharf – und suchen Schuldige.

spiegel.title: Anke Engelke in »Die Wahrheit über Social Media«: Bezahlt wird mit Lebenszeit, bisweilen sogar mit dem eigenen Leben
spiegel.description: Drei Viertel der Weltbevölkerung treiben sich bei TikTok, Instagram oder Snapchat herum – für Kochrezepte, Katzenvideos oder K-Pop-Clips. Eine ZDF-Doku zeigt die Abgründe dahinter. Und macht Anke Engelke zur Maschine.

spiegel.title: Krank mit Kind: Wenn Papa flachliegt und die Kleinen keine Pause kennen
spiegel.description: Wenn Sie richtig krank sind, ist nur eins noch schlimmer: richtig krank sein, gleichzeitig arbeiten ‒ und zu Hause springen die Kleinen rum. Über meinen chaotischen Versuch, mich einfach auszuruhen.

spiegel.title: Iran-Krieg und die USA: Fünf Gründe, warum es mit einem Deal nicht vorangeht
spiegel.description: Die Verhandlungen zwischen den USA und Iran stecken fest: Das Regime in Teheran wähnt sich in der besseren Position. Doch auch Donald Trump will keine Zugeständnisse machen. Wie es nun weitergehen könnte.

spiegel.title: Russlands Versuche, ukrainischen Drohnen abzuwehren: Die Zebra-Lkw brettern durch die Südukraine
spiegel.description: Russland bemalt seine Militärfahrzeuge wegen ukrainischer Drohnenschläge – und bedient sich wieder einmal im Tierreich. Ob das hilft, ist fraglich. Denn Moskaus Truppen stehen unter Druck.

spiegel.title: Japan: Überwachungskamera filmt Bärenangriff auf Fabrikgelände in Fukushima
spiegel.description: Tausende Bären dringen jedes Jahr in Japans Städte ein. Immer wieder kommt es zu Angriffen und sogar Todesfällen. Den jüngsten Vorfall in Fukushima hat eine Überwachungskamera gefilmt.

spiegel.title: 1860 München – 3. Liga: Traditionsclub muss schon wieder in der Regionalliga neu beginnen
spiegel.description: Es ist ein schmerzhaftes Déjà-vu für 1860 München. Investor Ismaik hat eine Finanzierungszusage nicht eingehalten, der Club stürzt schon wieder in die vierte Liga ab. Dies könnte Folgen bis in den Amateurfußball haben.

spiegel.title: Peter Thiel: Warum die Wiener Festwochen den Talk mit dem US-Milliardär absagten
spiegel.description: Der umstrittene US-Milliardär Peter Thiel sollte am Sonntag bei den Wiener Festwochen als Talkgast auftreten. Dann sagte Festivalintendant Milo Rau die Show ab. Hier erklärt er, warum.

spiegel.title: Eli Lilly: US-Pharmakonzern halbiert Milliardeninvestition in Deutschland
spiegel.description: Der US-Pharmariese Eli Lilly fährt die Investition für den geplanten Produktionsstandort auf den Mindestumfang herunter und verweist auf die Sparpläne der Bundesregierung. Auch ein deutscher Konzern stoppt Investitionen.

observador.title: Rússia acusa Ucrânia de ataque a autocarro que fez 8 mortos
observador.description: Rússia acusa Ucrânia de ter estado por detrás do ataque a um autocarro em Donetsk que fez 8 mortos e 11 feridos. O líder russo colocado naquela região indicou que o ataque teve lugar em Yenakiievo.

observador.title: Transformar a crise industrial numa oportunidade
observador.description: Portugal deve aproveitar a nova política industrial europeia para acelerar inovação, reduzir burocracia e reforçar competitividade, defende Rui Moreira, embaixador de Portugal na OCDE.

observador.title: As notícias das 21h
observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.title: "Israel tem mais controlo sobre Trump do que o contrário"
observador.description: João Albuquerque analisa a tensão entre Trump e Netanyahu perante as operações militares israelitas no Líbano e Irão. Ainda, o prestígio da entrada de Portugal no Conselho de Segurança da ONU.

observador.title: O recinto mais "verde" do Mundial que mora em Filadélfia
observador.description: Linc" não tem a arquitetura moderna de outros estádios da competição, que são mais tecnológicos. Por lá, o brilho das luzes fica para os protagonistas e os deste Mundial não serão exceção.

observador.title: Continente com concentração de pólen alta e baixa nas ilhas
observador.description: Todo o território continental estará, entre sexta-feira e 11 de junho, em risco elevado de concentração de pólen. Na Madeira e nos Açores, a concentração na atmosfera estará baixa.

observador.title: Metade dos alunos não realizou prova ModA devido à greve
observador.description: As provas de Português do 6.º ano estavam agendadas para esta quarta-feira, mas só 48% dos alunos realizaram a avaliação. Quem não a realizou devido à greve geral poderá fazê-la terça-feira.

observador.title: 20h. Greve. 6 pessoas detidas nos protestos junto à AR
observador.description: Já depois da manifestação da CGTP ter terminado um conjunto de pessoas provocou desacatos. Ainda, a partir de 2027, Portugal vai ocupar um dos lugares do Conselho de Segurança da ONU.

observador.title: Governo condena comportamentos "lamentáveis" de "alguns"
observador.description: António Leitão Amaro, ministro da Presidência do Conselho de Ministros, lamentou o que aconteceu em frente à Assembleia da República e agradeceu às forças de segurança.

observador.title: Passos quer resolver desafios que vão "além da lei laboral"
observador.description: Ex-primeiro-ministro está preocupado com desemprego tecnológico e produtividade da economia portuguesa. Em dia de greve, pediu mobilização do Governo, empresas e trabalhadores e "mudança de atitude".

observador.title: Greve Geral. Uma luta por algo que já morreu?
observador.description: Entre o "achómetro" dos sindicatos e o gelo do Governo, a ministra corre para os microfones para não perder o palco e a CGTP celebra um "sucesso" invisível no setor privado.

observador.title: As greves são os últimos suspiros do PCP
observador.description: Alberto Gonçalves comenta o significado da Greve Geral.

observador.title: "Temos, neste momento, uma espécie de eixo CGTP-Chega"
observador.description: Especialistas analisam a greve e a crise na representação sindical. No Parlamento, o Chega alinha-se com a CGTP contra a reforma laboral e o PCP procura uma prova de vida perante a baixa adesão.

observador.title: Fotogaleria. Violência junto à Assembleia da República
observador.description: Manifestantes lançaram garrafas de vidro na direção do dispositivo policial que garantia segurança junto ao Parlamento. PSP tentou afastar grupo das imediações do edifício.

observador.title: "Críticas de Passos foram um bocadinho too much"
observador.description: A deputada do PSD e presidente da comissão de Assuntos Constitucionais não gostou "do tom e do modo" das criticas de Passos a Luís Montenegro que diz até terem sido "grosseiras".

observador.title: 19h. Greve Geral. Manifestantes provocam desacatos com a PSP
observador.description: Foram também incendiados alguns caixotes do lixo. Ainda, Luís Montenegro desvaloriza a greve geral e critica a falta de contributos para o debate.

observador.title: Governo agarra greve para isolar funcionários públicos
observador.description: Governo insiste que setor privado trabalhou em peso -- incluindo quem será afetado pelo pacote laboral. Montenegro lembrou desvantagens práticas da greve, esperando que crie desgaste.

observador.title: Parlamento aprova na generalidade proposta para as heranças
observador.description: Governo viu ser aprovada, na generalidade, a proposta para as heranças indivisas. Também a IL conseguiu fazer aprovar a proposta para o cabeça-de-casal poder ser escolhido pela maioria dos herdeiros.

elpais.title: La UCO constata “al menos” tres reuniones de Leire Díez con la directora de la Guardia Civil, a la que instó a iniciar una “investigación interna” contra la Unidad
elpais.description: El sumario del ‘caso Leire’ recoge que la supuesta ‘fontanera’ del PSOE mantuvo además conversaciones de WhatsApp con Mercedes González, que esta borró

elpais.title: La Guardia Civil detecta gestiones de Leire Díez para buscar trabajo a la denunciante del fiscal Grinda mientras intentaba reactivar la causa
elpais.description: La mujer que emprendió acciones legales contra el fiscal declaró haberse reunido con Cerdán y la exmilitante en el PSOE para hablar del caso. Díez a Juan Francisco Serrano: “¿Insistes para que la empleen?"

elpais.description: Torró lamenta los “comportamientos de oportunistas y resentidos que han usado el nombre del partido en falso” en el ‘caso Leire’

elpais.title: “Llegaron los cambios”: más diversidad en la polémica Casita de Bad Bunny
elpais.description: Tras las críticas por la selección de mujeres normativas, en el tercer concierto en Madrid desconocidos de distintas tallas, edades y sexo bailan con famosos como el actor Noah Schnapp

elpais.description: Lo ganó todo con el Barça y tiene el récord de balones de oro. Hace cuatro años, en Qatar, se quitó la espina mundialista. En vísperas de su sexta Copa del Mundo, suma a su lista de galardones el Premio Princesa de Asturias de los Deportes 2026

elpais.title: La guerra de Estados Unidos e Israel contra Irán, en directo | Trump ve posible que el acuerdo de paz con Irán se alcance el fin de semana

elpais.description: El presidente expresa su determinación de culminar la legislatura en la reunión anual del Cercle d’Economia

elpais.title: El juez del ‘caso Plus Ultra’ pide una tasación preliminar de las joyas de Zapatero
elpais.description: El magistrado Calama quiere saber “su naturaleza, autenticidad y valor económico” además del “fabricante”

elpais.title: El PP acepta en Castilla y León la “prioridad nacional” y cede a Vox la política medioambiental y cultural
elpais.description: Los ultras asumen una vicepresidencia y tres consejerías para investir a Mañueco presidente de un gobierno de coalición. El PP se queda la gestión de los incendios

elpais.title: La Justicia francesa autoriza la entrega a España de Josu Ternera para juzgarlo por su presunta responsabilidad como jefe de ETA
elpais.description: El Tribunal de Apelación acepta la euroorden española, aunque queda a la espera de que se resuelva la última causa que el etarra tiene en Francia, ya juzgada, cuyo fallo se dictará el 2 de julio

elpais.title: Meliá también cede ante la presión de Trump y abandona la gestión de 15 hoteles en Cuba
elpais.description: La decisión, comunicada a la CNMV, se produce tan solo un día después de que Iberostar anunciara que retira su marca a 12 establecimientos en la isla

republika.description: Al Najjar ha perso moglie e 4 figli nel 2024: aveva già il permesso per studiare a Tor Vergata. Le autorità italiane seguono il caso

republika.description: Cinquant’anni di Repubblica. Ogni giovedì (fino all’uscita successiva) i lettori potranno votare la prima pagina di un decennio. Questa settimana, fatti, personaggi e grandi avvenimenti raccontati dal 2006 al 2015

republika.description: La “Venezia del Nord” celebrata da Dostoevskij è stata scelta dal leader del Cremlino per la sua Davos. E i bombardamenti ucraini di oggi sono uno sfregio. Una sorta di “Delitto e Castigo”

republika.description: Mozione a prima firma 5stelle condivisa con Pd, Avs e Iv. Chiesta anche "una revisione integrale del patto di stabilità". La destra inverte l’ordine dei lavori: prima il nucleare. Protesta delle opposizioni: dittatura della maggioranza

republika.description: Il procuratore capo D’Alessio: “Non c’è collaborazione, dobbiamo sfaldare il muro di omertà”. Un carabiniere pochi istanti prima aveva redarguito i due ventenni pachistani, poi il rogo e i quattro morti

republika.description: L’Italia resta in procedura per deficit eccessivo. Dalla scuola alla sanità, allo sfruttamento del lavoro. Ecco tutte le raccomandazioni nel pacchetto primaverile della Commissione. Meloni: “Risultato molto importante”

nyt.title: Out of Time to Delay, House to Vote on Trump’s Power to Continue War in Iran
nyt.description: A measure to direct the president to halt U.S. engagement in Iran had been on track to pass in late May, but Republican leaders postponed action. They have run out of time to delay the vote.

nyt.title: ‘Infuriated’ Former Judges Take on Trump
nyt.description: Critics say it is unseemly for retired judges to trade on the prestige of their former positions.

nyt.title: The Narrow Path to a Democratic Senate Runs Through Very Red States
nyt.description: Democrats cheer there is a way, even as new worries emerge over whether Graham Platner can flip a Maine seat. Republicans remain confident they will prevail in Texas, Iowa and Alaska.

nyt.title: Trump Administration Fights Court Order to Refund Some Tariffs
nyt.description: The administration has started to repay some of the money, but has signaled it may make it harder for certain businesses to claim the full amount they are owed.

nyt.title: Trump Administration Turns to a New Rationale to Justify Old Tariffs
nyt.description: The administration has settled on a more legally and politically durable way to impose tariffs, but some say the focus on forced labor is merely a pretext for protectionism.

nyt.title: How Taylor Swift Writes a Song, In Her Own Words
nyt.description: The artist shares stories behind some of her biggest hits, her love of a “rant bridge” and how life in the public eye informs the stories she tells in her songs.

nyt.title: Bari Weiss Speaks on Scott Pelley’s ’60 Minutes’ Firing: ‘That’s the Path That He Chose’
nyt.description: In her first public comments on the firing, Ms. Weiss, the CBS News editor in chief, said that the longtime correspondent had “broken” the trust in the newsroom.

nyt.title: See the Clashes Between ICE and Protesters in New Jersey
nyt.description: Demonstrations outside the Delaney Hall immigrant detention center have at times turned violent, with the authorities deploying tear gas and wielding batons as protesters resisted calls to disperse.

nyt.title: Mullin Says ICE Training Going Back to ‘Regular Standards’
nyt.description: The immigration agency had apparently cut training requirements as a part of its enforcement push over the past year.

nyt.title: In Apparent Reversal, Mullin Says Abrego Garcia Could Be Deported to Costa Rica
nyt.description: Kilmar Armando Abrego Garcia has long said he would willingly go to Costa Rica. His lawyers sent the new homeland security secretary’s comments to the judge handling his deportation case.

nyt.title: A New Play, ‘Kenrex,’ Revisits the Story of a Bully’s Unsolved Murder
nyt.description: A man was shot dead surrounded by witnesses in Skidmore, Mo., but no one was ever prosecuted. Now that act of vigilante justice has inspired the play “Kenrex.”

nyt.title: For Knicks’ Owner James Dolan, a Title Might Finally Stop Some Boos
nyt.description: James Dolan, the longtime owner of the N.B.A. team, has faced years of jeers. Could a championship change all that?

nyt.title: Want Courtside Seats for the Knicks? Be Rich, Famous and a Die-Hard Fan.
nyt.description: Prime tickets on the floor for the N.B.A. Finals are coveted and very hard to get. The No. 1 requirement: You must love the Knicks.

nyt.title: An Uncertain Path for Americans Exposed to Ebola
nyt.description: Despite long-established procedures for bringing Americans home for monitoring and treatment, the Trump administration has not said that it will allow those at risk of Ebola back into the country.

nyt.title: Charleston’s Charm Hides Bloody History of Revolutionary War in South Carolina
nyt.description: Some of the fiercest battles took place in South Carolina, but its part in the fight for independence is often overlooked. Our reporter found history, myths, beauty and contradiction across the Lowcountry landscapes.

nyt.description: It just needs to be given the chance.

npr.title: Trump confirms calling Netanyahu 'crazy,' says they still get along
npr.description: The president also acknowledged that he cursed at the Israeli leader in a heated phone call in which he told Benjamin Netanyahu not to bomb the Lebanese capital Beirut.

npr.title: Greetings from Porto, whose lanes are lined with colorful textiles

new-sci.title: Ötzi's frozen remains may harbour metabolically active microbes
new-sci.description: Researchers studying a 5300-year-old mummified man have identified bacteria that lived in his gut when he was alive, as well as cold-tolerant fungi that colonised his body after death

new-sci.title: Why you need to future proof your brain in middle age and how to start
new-sci.description: Ages 40 to 65 see a period of turmoil in the brain that has previously been overlooked. But identifying problems during this time can protect your cognitive health for decades to come

new-sci.title: How the electromagnetic spectrum opened our eyes to the universe
new-sci.description: Our understanding of the electromagnetic spectrum goes back to Isaac Newton, but astronomers are still finding new ways to employ it. Astrophysicist Emma Chapman explores how much these invisible waves can reveal to us about the cosmos – and whether they might show us that we’re not alone

new-sci.title: The best new popular science books of June 2026

new-sci.description: From dementia to heart attacks, hearing loss has been linked to a wide range of effects across the body, and the condition is on the rise. Fortunately, we're learning how best to safeguard this crucial sense and how we might be able to reverse the damage

new-sci.title: Hidden store of manganese may have helped Earth get its oxygen
new-sci.description: Computer simulations have uncovered a new manganese compound that could exist deep in Earth’s mantle and may be connected to the process that gave our atmosphere oxygen

new-sci.title: New Scientist recommends Togetherness, a radical new view of life
new-sci.description: An exploration of how biological cooperation underpins all life - and why we’ve overlooked its power until now - makes thrilling reading, finds Penny Sarchet

new-sci.description: Mathematicians are stunned at the progress AI is making in solving advanced problems, leaving some questioning whether there will still be room for humans

new-sci.title: 'Transformative' pancreatic cancer drug doubles survival time
new-sci.description: People with advanced pancreatic cancer taking an experimental daily pill lived nearly twice as long as those receiving chemotherapy infusions

new-sci.title: How human error became a weapon against large language models
new-sci.description: Alan Turing proposed a test for machine intelligence: could a computer convince a human it was human? We have begun conducting the same test on ourselves, writes Max Moser

new-sci.title: Do turmeric and curcumin have any actual health benefits?
new-sci.description: Turmeric is heralded for its anti-cancer and anti-inflammatory properties, but columnist Alice Klein finds that the evidence for this is shaky. Taking high doses of its curcumin extract in supplement form can be risky

new-sci.title: Huge study of Alzheimer’s genetics identifies new drug targets
new-sci.description: Almost 50 more genes have been flagged as being linked to Alzheimer’s, along with changes in activity in crucial cells that disappear as dementia progresses

new-sci.title: Capitalism has warped our understanding of ecology and life’s origins
new-sci.description: The ideas of survival of the fittest and winning at all costs are closely entwinned with Darwinism, but they shouldn’t be. A rethink from a more communal perspective is in order

phys-org.title: Integrating citizen science with experimental data uncovers how switchgrass adapts flowering by region
phys-org.description: In its native habitat, switchgrass flowered earlier when growing farther north. In experiments with diverse genetic samples, it flowered earlier in the south.

phys-org.title: Brightness 'gap' in ancient star cluster reveals missing red dwarfs
phys-org.description: Scientists from the Space Telescope Science Institute (STScI) in Baltimore, Maryland, sought to study one stellar subject and ended up finding something even more exciting. The team's results published today in Astronomy & Astrophysics.

phys-org.title: Sunrise III data release opens rare high-altitude solar views that could sharpen space weather forecasts
phys-org.description: Close to 100 scientists from all over Europe, the United States, and Japan are gathering this week at the Institute for Solar Physics (KIS) in Freiburg to present and discuss the first scientific results from the successful third flight of the balloon-borne solar observatory SUNRISE. KIS is a key contributor to the SUNRISE project. The meeting marks a milestone in the study of the sun by bringing together researchers from all over the world who are analyzing unprecedented new data gathered by th

phys-org.title: Dogs respond to human tone without words, hinting at communication older than language
phys-org.description: Humans can communicate various instructions to dogs without using actual words—simply by modulating the tone of their voice, a new study from ELTE University's Department of Ethology shows. By repeating the nonsense syllable 'bü' in different intonations, humans successfully signaled "Yes," "No," "Here," and "There" and, remarkably, dogs responded correctly, despite receiving no prior training. The findings reveal ancient acoustic codes, interpretable across species, that predate

phys-org.title: Nanomagnets control diamond qubits, pointing to more scalable quantum hardware
phys-org.description: Quantum computing, once only a theoretical possibility, promises to deliver faster, more energy-efficient computers—but only if scientists can build and scale the hardware needed to run the machines. New research from Virginia Commonwealth University brings scientists one small step closer to quantum computing at a practical scale, which could help dramatically reduce energy usage and computing times in some industries.

phys-org.title: Attribution constraints reveal stronger future intensification of the upper‑level Hadley circulation
phys-org.description: The Hadley circulation, a key atmospheric conveyor belt transporting heat and moisture from the tropics to the subtropics, directly influences subtropical aridity, the positions of tropical rainfall belts, and extreme weather risks. However, climate models have long shown inconsistencies in simulating its upper-level intensity (UP-HCI), undermining the reliability of future projections.

phys-org.title: Arctic river deltas face rising climate pressure while holding vast frozen carbon reserves
phys-org.description: Many rivers flow into the Arctic Ocean north of the Arctic Circle—including the Lena in Siberia and the Mackenzie River in Canada. The deltas of these large and small rivers store large amounts of carbon, which is bound there in frozen soils and sediments. Climate change, however, is destabilizing the deltas from the ocean and land side and also from the air.

phys-org.title: Open-source software unlocks rapid DNA structure generation and analysis in one workflow
phys-org.description: Computational chemists at the University of Amsterdam's Van 't Hoff Institute for Molecular Sciences have developed a comprehensive software suite to create accurate models of DNA in biomolecular assemblies. Called MDNA, the user-friendly molecular modeling toolkit helps biochemists, molecular biologists, bioinformaticians, and biophysicists to visualize and analyze DNA structures and perform accurate simulations.

phys-org.title: Social networks outsmart cognitive biases: How herding in networks makes populations more rational
phys-org.description: In 2010, the New York City-based restaurant Serendipity 3 revealed its $69 hot dog, winning the Guinness World Record for the world's most expensive hot dog. Served on a toasted pretzel roll with truffle butter and covered in foie gras, the award-winning hot dog made the restaurant's $18 cheeseburger seem like a steal. That's the point, says Professor Damon Centola of the Annenberg School for Communication at the University of Pennsylvania.

phys-org.title: Giant fan-shaped structure found under East Antarctica
phys-org.description: An international team of researchers including our Department of Geography has discovered a vast geological structure hidden beneath the East Antarctic Ice Sheet. The findings are published in the journal Nature Geoscience.

phys-org.title: Real-time fish interaction enlarges young guppy brains, while screen time falls short
phys-org.description: Young guppies who were able to see and interact with live fish developed larger brains than guppies who only saw other fish on a screen. This is shown in a new study from Stockholm University, published in Biology Letters. The findings suggest that live social interaction in real time may be important for brain development.

phys-org.title: Cleaner recycling method unlocks reusable plastics from mixed packaging
phys-org.description: Scientists from Nanyang Technological University, Singapore (NTU Singapore) have developed a new method to recycle mixed plastic packaging without using harmful chemical solvents—an approach that could make one of the world's most difficult waste streams significantly easier to handle.

phys-org.title: Aluminum oxide's irregular atomic surface explains its low reactivity
phys-org.description: Why do certain surfaces behave very differently from what theoretical calculations suggest? Scientists long assumed that the aluminum oxide surface should be highly reactive and capable of splitting water molecules. In experiments, however, this behavior is barely observed.

phys-org.title: Warming unlocks ancient carbon in Tibetan permafrost, triggering climate tipping point
phys-org.description: A new study in Nature Communications  finds a critical climate tipping point in Tibetan permafrost ecosystems. Warming of 2–4 degrees Celsius triggers a self-reinforcing cycle of carbon release that could significantly accelerate climate change, according to the work.

phys-org.title: Out-of-plane ice bridges reveal new way to suppress frost spreading
phys-org.description: A research team led by Professor Nenad Miljkovic in The Grainger College of Engineering at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign has published a breakthrough study in Nature Physics. The work reports the first experimental discovery of a previously unknown frost propagation mechanism—a "suspended ice bridge"—offering new pathways for anti-frosting surface design.

phys-org.title: 8 out of 10 northern fulmar seabirds have plastic in their stomachs, finds study
phys-org.description: Plastic pollution is widespread in the world's oceans. A new study of northern fulmars from the North Atlantic shows that plastic pollution is also common in northern marine areas. The research is published in the journal Marine Pollution Bulletin.

phys-org.title: 'Don't scare the cat!' Engineers find smarter way to measure quantum systems
phys-org.description: UNSW Sydney engineers have riffed on the famous Schrödinger's cat analogy to demonstrate a more efficient way to eliminate errors in quantum computing.

phys-org.title: Greenland shark genome reveals clues to 400-year lifespan
phys-org.description: The first comprehensive map of nearly the entire Greenland shark genome is beginning to reveal some of the genetic clues behind its incredibly long life. The work could one day help scientists develop new cures and treatments for cancer and other age-related diseases.

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

undark.title: Book Review: Within Our Cells, the Miracle of Constant Mutation
undark.description: Our cells are constantly mutating in a battle for the survival of the fittest that is raging inside us daily, Roxanne Khamsi writes in “Beyond Inheritance.” Many of these mutations are harmless, others are cellular deviants that lead to disease, and remarkably, some can actually self-correct.

undark.title: The Six-Week Postpartum Checkup Comes Too Late
undark.description: In the U.S., maternity care generally ends with a checkup scheduled six weeks after giving birth. This single doctor’s appointment may be efficient for billing and discharge protocols, but the timing reflects the structure of the health care system more than the reality of maternal recovery.

undark.title: Book Review:  The Case for Making Data-Driven Decisions
undark.description: In “Beyond Belief: How Evidence Shows What Really Works,” science journalist Helen Pearson profiles a group of people working in medicine and other fields who became leaders of the worldwide evidence movement, which encourages the use of data from rigorous research to direct treatments, policies, and plans.

undark.title: What the Hantavirus Story Reveals About Medical Mistrust
undark.description: The reaction to an outbreak of hantavirus on a cruise ship reveals a story about mistrust in medicine and public health. In the U.S., hantavirus disproportionately kills Native Americans. A doctor who works at a hospital on Navajo Nation writes that such mistrust always lands hardest on the most vulnerable.

undark.title: Book Review: The Mind-Boggling Science of Enormous Numbers
undark.description: In “Huge Numbers: A Story of Counting Ambitiously, From 4½ to Fish 7,” mathematician Richard Elwes shows off his love of all things numeric, and, in particular, shines a spotlight on some of the largest numbers humans have ever contemplated, and the much larger numbers that await those who seek them out.

undark.title: When Scientific Arguments Obscure Moral Ones, Democracy Suffers
undark.description: The Pentagon’s new vaccine policy values individual choice over public health. Which of these values should be prioritized is a legitimate subject for democratic debate. But when experts respond to moral arguments animating policy decisions by reiterating facts, it undermines debate and fuels divisiveness.

undark.title: Book Review: The Life and Struggles of a Conservation Pioneer
undark.description: Over a career of many decades, George Schaller laid the groundwork for the field of conservation biology, and his pioneering research likely saved numerous species from extinction. In “Homesick for a World Unknown,” Miriam Horn documents his triumphs, challenges, and setbacks in meticulous detail.

undark.title: Medicine’s Move Toward Race-Neutral Risk Assessments
undark.description: Earlier this year, new guidelines were released for doctors assessing a patient’s risk for heart disease. The guidelines take a race-neutral and patient-informed approach that’s rooted in up-to-date science, one doctor writes, and offer a glimpse of a future in which health equity is the standard in medicine.

undark.title: In Coal Country, Black Lung Surges as Federal Protections Stall
undark.description: While the Trump administration is directing hundreds of millions of dollars to coal projects, miners in Appalachia are suffering from a resurgence of black lung disease. But industry pushback is delaying federal rules that would reduce miners’ exposure to deadly silica dust.

proj-syn.title: Democracy vs. Data Centers
proj-syn.description: As tech companies race to build data centers, communities and lawmakers across the United States are pushing back. Industry leaders frame local opposition as a threat to American competitiveness, but China’s experience shows that unchecked expansion carries serious risks of its own.

proj-syn.title: The Right Incentives for Climate Action
proj-syn.description: As the closure of the Strait of Hormuz continues to disrupt global oil and gas flows, countries are increasingly focusing on short-term energy priorities to the detriment of long-term decarbonization goals. In such a context, the difficult task of designing climate policies that realign incentives takes on new importance.

proj-syn.title: The US and India Have Become Regional Rivals
proj-syn.description: While the US views India as a counterweight to China in Asia, it balks at the idea of Indian regional dominance, preferring a pluralistic order. The Trump administration has gone further by pursuing close ties with Pakistan, apparently hoping that the US and India can remain global partners.

proj-syn.title: Digital Sovereignty Is in the Fine Print
proj-syn.description: Despite efforts to build their own digital industries and infrastructure, most countries remain dependent on American tech firms for the provision of core government services. But government officials can tip the balance of bargaining power by attaching certain standardized provisions to public procurement and services contracts.

proj-syn.title: Trump Wants to Privatize His Presidential Records
proj-syn.description: By enacting the Presidential Records Act in response to Richard Nixon’s malfeasance, the US Congress created a process to limit abuse of power and ensure accountability. Like Nixon, Donald Trump seems determined to avoid accountability, which has led his Justice Department to argue—poorly—that the PRA is unconstitutional.

proj-syn.title: British Steel Needs a Transformation, Not a Bailout
proj-syn.description: The recent revival of industrial policy offers an opportunity to break the old pattern whereby economic risks are socialized while rewards remain privatized. In addition to attaching meaningful conditionalities to public support, governments must invest in the state capacity required to govern strategic sectors well.

proj-syn.title: How to Encourage Deceased Organ Donation
proj-syn.description: Developing countries facing organ shortages often search for complex solutions, such as sweeping legal reforms. But Tunisia’s experience suggests a much simpler first step: awareness-raising sessions where doctors explain how the transplant system works, and people share their fears and concerns.

proj-syn.title: Building Alliances of America’s Allies
proj-syn.description: In a world in which the US cannot be counted on as it once was, the objective is not stability at any price, but rather stability on terms consistent with national and Western interests. This is achievable, but only if the friends of the US recognize the new reality and act individually and collectively to meet the challenge.

proj-syn.title: The Promise and Limits of African Data Sovereignty
proj-syn.description: African countries are recognizing that no matter how well-designed their data-protection regulations are, their sovereignty over US-based Big Tech firms ends at the boundary between subsidiary and parent. Overcoming this barrier will require a level of coordination that the continent has yet to achieve.

proj-syn.title: The AI Economy’s Permanent Underclass
proj-syn.description: AI is transforming the global economy while widening the gap between technological winners and losers. Governments that fail to secure a place in the AI supply chain may find themselves confronting mass job displacement without the tax revenues or state capacity needed to contain the social and political fallout.

proj-syn.title: The Rape of Venezuela
proj-syn.description: Venezuela’s oil production is rising, yet its currency is depreciating, inflation is accelerating, and foreign exchange remains scarce. The disconnect reflects a political economy built on private dealmaking and a mutually beneficial alliance between ruling elites and US President Donald Trump’s acolytes.

proj-syn.title: The One Man Who Could Give Trump Middle East Peace
proj-syn.description: With a large majority of UN member states recognizing Palestine on the 1967 lines, there is a clear international blueprint for creating an independent Palestinian state alongside Israel. What has been missing is credible Palestinian leadership of the kind that the imprisoned politician Marwan Barghouti could provide.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s Nuclear Options
proj-syn.description: The risks raised by nuclear weapons remain as potent as ever, but the institutional framework that mitigated them has been severely eroded. The task now is to prevent deterrence from giving way to proliferation—which, for Europe, means building conventional capabilities, keeping the US engaged, and upholding restraint.

proj-syn.title: The Intelligence That AI Is Missing
proj-syn.description: For AI to simplify humans’ complex social and professional lives, it cannot just give tidy answers based on whatever the internet has to say about our values. It will need the capacity to account for our relational commitments, which are typically grounded in personal identity, experience, and culture.

proj-syn.title: Why Isn’t Europe Poorer Than the US?
proj-syn.description: Nobel laureate Paul Krugman has a point when he says that European living standards have largely kept pace with those in the US, despite flagging growth and innovation. But this will not remain true indefinitely: restoring Europe's ability to compete at the technological frontier remains essential to its future well-being.

proj-syn.title: The Real Choice Confronting Developing Countries
proj-syn.description: Lost in the debate about whether developing countries should pursue manufacturing- or services-led growth is the potential for new AI tools to make even informal workers far more productive. If governments can broaden access to such technologies, they no longer need to choose between strategies.

proj-syn.title: India’s Great Political Realignment
proj-syn.description: In recent years, the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party’s focus on religious identity, together with its “purification” of voter rolls, has created a more binary—and potentially volatile—political landscape, where elections increasingly reflect ethno-religious identity. This month’s elections in five states largely confirmed this trend.

proj-syn.title: Central Banking in an Age of Global Supply Shocks
proj-syn.description: The core assumptions underlying the decades-old inflation-targeting orthodoxy have proven to be unfit for a geopolitically fragmented world characterized by frequent supply-side disruptions. Under such conditions, central banks' traditional monetary policies are only as effective as markets believe them to be.
